basis: User-authorized absent-trailing-cell evolution; unchanged API/limits and historical documented scalar profile. No new input-cleanup semantics.

globalProtocol.execution: Only after explicit closed-author handoff, from authenticated committed regular archive. Large cases each run in an isolated bounded product child, never native.
globalProtocol.interpretation: V8 heap cap is not an RSS guarantee. Deadline, cap, signal, premature exit, or forced group cleanup is failure, never expected budget refusal or PASS. No performance comparison.
globalProtocol.capture: Record exact argv, override limits, generator and input hash, status, stdout/stderr bytes or bounded stream hash+length+prefix, effects, write sizes/counts, resource admission/return events and child close/group retirement. Never allocate a rectangular oracle or giant expected string.
globalProtocol.allocation: Bound product child even if instrumentation is bypassed. Guard padding repeat/allocation and record arrays in that child only; include deliberately unsafe synthetic negative controls. Do not infer absence of rectangular allocation from elapsed time or successful output alone.
globalProtocol.work: Do not guess implementation-specific exact maxSteps totals. Small sufficient-budget exact controls and deliberately insufficient budgets are separate assertions. No uncharged rows-times-absent-columns scan is permitted, including zero-byte output.
globalProtocol.terminology: There is no maxColumns option: maxFields limits actual fields per record, maxCells cumulative parsed fields. Absent rendered cells must not materialize a rows-times-maxFields matrix.
globalProtocol.diagnostics: For failures retain original diagnostics and status; require nonzero and bounded diagnostic bytes, not invented message spelling. Completed awaited sink writes may remain a prefix. Input/decode failures must precede layout output.
globalProtocol.notInScope: No S38 reclassification, assertion migration, opaque-return contract audit, source edits, public integration, new dependencies or product runs during preparation.

schedules.name: ragged-output-exact-boundary

runs.expect: nonzero; stdout is a prefix of exact success and at most 39 bytes

schedules.negativeControl: Old no-absent-padding output must fail byte equality; accepting 40 bytes under cap39 must fail.

schedules.name: padding-preallocation-not-posthoc-truncation
schedules.expect: Nonzero, output <=1024; the first row needs 4095 spaces plus separator before LF. Any padding allocation/repeat exceeding remaining output budget is rejected before allocation, even if later slicing could hide it. Bounded incremental admission is allowed.
schedules.negativeControl: Synthetic allocate-padding-then-check implementation must trip isolated allocation observer, not pass solely for final capped bytes.

schedules.name: sparse-ragged-low-output-cap
schedules.generator: First record x plus ':' repeated 1023 plus LF; then 'x\n' repeated 19999. Stream chunks <=4096 bytes.
schedules.expect: Nonzero with <=4096 output; no rectangular row expansion or row-width padding string allocated before budget refusal. Input stays below default rows/cells/bytes bounds.
schedules.negativeControl: Rectangular synthetic allocator must fail child allocation/heap guard even if it would emit identical bytes.

schedules.name: zero-output-absent-columns-no-quadratic-scan
schedules.expect: Either exact successful stream through bounded aggregate handling, or explicit maxSteps refusal with a bounded exact-output prefix. Uncharged 20,480,000-slot traversal is failure, not permitted zero-output work. A refusal is resource-safety success only, never byte-layout success.
schedules.negativeControl: Unchecked synthetic zero-byte rectangular scanner must be detected by work instrumentation or isolated child failure, not credited by output hash.

schedules.name: zero-width-columns-small-exact
schedules.expect: Exact success including one space padding the explicit empty first field to global first-column width; absent zero-width tails add no separator bytes.
schedules.negativeControl: Skipping explicit-empty first-column padding must fail; manufacturing delimiters for empty -o must fail.

schedules.name: display-zero-does-not-mean-byte-zero
schedules.negativeControl: Charging combining scalars as zero bytes must fail the cap7 case.

schedules.name: multibyte-separator-byte-budget
schedules.negativeControl: Budget by separator display width instead of UTF-8 bytes must fail.

schedules.name: cumulative-work-before-layout
schedules.expect: Work cannot reset per row. Record counters and refusal stage; do not infer precise charge formula.
schedules.negativeControl: Per-record reset or silently ignoring maxSteps must fail.

schedules.name: actual-fields-cells-rows-input-independent

runs.expect: exact success; absent rendering cells are not parsed cells

schedules.negativeControl: Charging a materialized six-cell rectangle against maxCells4 is not a substitute for preserving the four parsed cells.

schedules.name: padding-writes-bounded-and-backpressured
schedules.schedule: Hold the first padding-bearing sink write; advance deterministic microtask turns; verify no second concurrent write or public settlement. Release gate, require exact stream computed incrementally from column widths [32768,1].
schedules.expect: Every observed sink write <=65536 bytes for this bounded fixture, sequential awaited writes; output 65543 bytes. This is a fixture safety ceiling, not an output guarantee of maxChunkBytes (an input limit). Future harness records actual maximum padding chunk size without inventing a public output-chunk option.
schedules.negativeControl: Fire-and-forget writer or over-ceiling single padding write must fail.

schedules.name: cancel-during-padding-and-owned-return
schedules.schedule: Two separate gates, not an impossible simultaneous lease: (A) after input retires normally, hold a padding sink write and abort with unique object; observe late resolve/reject without further writes; (B) while an owned VFS next remains pending after the ragged bytes, abort and hold its cooperative return, then release it. Register cleanup synchronously before acquisition in both direct contexts; invoke overlapping registered/finally cleanup.
schedules.expect: Exact abort identity. In B result remains pending until the registered owned return gate releases, one underlying return; no new acquisitions/writes after abort admission closes. In A do not invent an owned lease for an opaque pending sink. Observe late rejections and no owned child/resource leak; do not substitute borrowed opaque external stdin.
schedules.negativeControl: Early settlement before registered return, duplicate return, or starting post-abort padding write must fail.

schedules.name: padding-sink-partial-failure-prefix
schedules.schedule: Record successful writes; sink rejects on the first write containing padding for the ragged second row, with a unique failure object. Retain rejected attempted bytes separately from completed effects.
schedules.expect: Fail according to existing direct-context sink contract (nonzero handled status if diagnostic succeeds; propagate diagnostic-sink failure); completed bytes are a prefix of the exact success string, no later stdout writes, owned cleanup exactly once. Run sinks that reject before and after recording attempted effects; distinguish both explicitly.
schedules.negativeControl: Continuing after sink rejection or claiming attempted bytes were completed must fail.

schedules.name: control-invalid-utf8-no-padding-publication
schedules.expect: Strict profile nonzero, no layout output, bounded diagnostics and cooperative owned cleanup. Split malformed sequence across producer chunks in a second schedule; neither native acceptance nor padding change permits it.
schedules.negativeControl: Replacement-decoding, accepting NUL/ZWJ, or publishing the first row before validation must fail.

schedules.name: reused-byte-source-and-final-partial
schedules.schedule: Yield transient Buffer views from a single reused buffer; split at delimiters and UTF-8 boundaries in companion P10. Mutate backing buffer before each next and at EOF/return. Compare ordinary and reused producer captures, including final partial record.
schedules.expect: Exact retained bytes copied before producer advance/finalization, no arbitrary concurrent-mutation claim.
schedules.negativeControl: Retaining subarray views must fail when earlier rows are overwritten.
